result.description:
We are looking for an experienced and strategic Cyber Security Architect to lead the design and implementation of advanced security systems across enterprise environments. This role is responsible for developing security architecture frameworks, identifying cyber risks, and delivering secure-by-design solutions that align with business goals and compliance standards.
The ideal candidate will have deep expertise in security controls, cloud security, enterprise infrastructure, and governance frameworks, and will play a lead role in defining the organisation’s cyber defence strategy.
Key Responsibilities:
Design, develop, and maintain enterprise-wide security architecture covering infrastructure, applications, data, identity, and cloud platforms.
Lead security assessments, threat modelling, and risk analysis during the solution design phase for new systems or services.
Define and implement security reference architectures and ensure adherence to frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, and Zero Trust.
Oversee the integration of security tools and controls across network, endpoint, identity, and cloud layers (e.g., SIEM, EDR, CASB, IAM, firewalls).
Collaborate with software engineers, DevOps teams, and cloud architects to embed security-by-design principles in SDLC and CI/CD pipelines.
Review security incidents and recommend architectural enhancements to improve resilience and reduce attack surfaces.
Develop and maintain policies, procedures, and architectural documentation, ensuring alignment with internal governance and external regulatory requirements.
Act as a key stakeholder in incident response planning, disaster recovery architecture, and business continuity strategies.
Provide technical guidance and leadership to security engineering and operations teams, and advise executives on cyber risks.
Liaise with vendors, regulators, and third parties to ensure security architecture is compliant and up to date with emerging threats.
Required Qualifications & Skills:
Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Cyber Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related discipline.
5+ years of experience in cyber security with at least 2–3 years in security architecture or design roles.
Strong understanding of network security, encryption, identity management, cloud security (AWS/Azure/GCP), and endpoint protection.
Proficiency with security technologies such as SIEM, IDS/IPS, IAM, MFA, EDR, firewalls, VPNs, and vulnerability scanners.
Hands-on experience designing secure systems in cloud-native, hybrid, or on-premise environments.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity standards and frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, ASD Essential Eight, OWASP).
Excellent documentation, stakeholder engagement, and risk communication skills.
Desirable:
Relevant certifications such as SABSA, CISSP, CISM, AWS Security, Azure Security Engineer, TOGAF.
Experience in Zero Trust Architecture, DevSecOps, or secure multi-cloud environments.
Background in regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, critical infrastructure, or government.
Familiarity with threat intelligence platforms, security automation, and SOAR tools.

Permanent Residents (PR) and Australian Citizens are eligible to apply
Job Type: Full-time
Salary: $70,000 to $120,000 per year + Super

About the Role:
We are seeking an experienced and passionate Butcher to join a premium, family-owned meat producer renowned for its commitment to ethical farming, sustainable practices, and high-quality, pasture-raised meats. Our client takes pride in delivering artisanal cuts, smallgoods, and specialty products that reflect traditional butchery techniques with a modern twist.
This is a hands-on role where you will be responsible for preparing, processing, and presenting a range of high-quality meats while maintaining the highest standards of hygiene, craftsmanship, and customer service. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of whole carcass butchery, smallgoods production, and a dedication to sustainable, ethically sourced meat.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Meat Preparation & Processing:
• Expertly break down whole carcasses, debone, trim, and portion meat into retail-ready cuts while minimizing waste.
• Prepare specialty cuts, including crumbed, marinated, and cured meats, using traditional techniques and premium ingredients.
• Craft smallgoods such as sausages, cured meats, and smoked products using artisanal methods and high-quality seasonings.

Machine Operation & Production:
• Operate and maintain butchery equipment, including mincers, grinders, tenderisers, and sausage fillers, ensuring efficiency and safety.
• Manage smoking chambers, curing vats, and cooking kettles to produce smoked and cooked smallgoods with precision.
• Prepare custom spice blends, brines, and marinades to enhance flavour profiles in line with artisanal standards.

Customer Service & Product Knowledge:
• Provide expert advice to customers on meat selection, cooking techniques, and optimal cuts for different culinary uses.
• Assist in menu planning and cost estimation for special orders, bulk purchases, and wholesale requirements.
• Maintain an attractive and hygienic display of products, always ensure freshness and quality.

Skills & Experience Required:
• Minimum 1+ years of experience in butchery, preferably within a premium or artisanal meat production environment.
• Relevant Certificate III Qualification related to the field advertised.
• Proficiency in whole carcass butchery, smallgoods production, and specialty cuts (e.g., dry-aged, cured, smoked).
• Strong knowledge of meat safety, hygiene standards, and HACCP compliance.
• Ability to operate butchery machinery and tools with precision and care.
• Excellent customer service skills with a passion for educating clients on quality meats.
• Experience in sustainable or pasture-raised meat production is highly regarded.

Why Apply?
This is a fantastic opportunity to work with a respected producer dedicated to ethical farming, sustainability, and superior-quality meats. You’ll be part of a team that values craftsmanship, innovation, and a deep respect for traditional butchery methods.

If you’re a skilled butcher with a passion for quality and sustainability, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

result.description:
Alice Springs College of Australia Pty. Ltd. (ASCA) focuses on fostering independent thought and effective communication in students through quality-driven instruction that offers leadership opportunities and experiential learning in Australia.  


ASCA is seeking a dedicated and experienced Office Manager to join our team on a full-time basis at our main campus in Burwood NSW. This role is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operations of the institute and ensuring the organisation runs smoothly, efficiently, and professionally.  The base salary ranges from $80,000 to $85,000 plus superannuation, depending on qualifications, skills, and experience.  Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.


Skills Requirement: You should have a minimum Diploma in Management, Leadership, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience.   At least one year of relevant experience is required.  In addition, you should possess sound organisational and time-management skills, and proficiency in office management systems and software applications.


Key tasks for this role include: 
•	Oversee the day-to-day operations of the campus to ensure a smooth, efficient, and professional working environment.
•	Develop, implement, and maintain office policies, procedures, and administrative systems to support operational effectiveness and compliance.
•	Manage procurement activities, inventory control, and the maintenance of office supplies and equipment.
•	Coordinate campus facilities, including repairs, maintenance, and essential service providers.
•	Provide high-level administrative support to senior management and assist with regulatory and compliance requirements.
•	Maintain accurate records, databases, and filing systems, ensuring data integrity and confidentiality.
•	Prepare operational reports, correspondence, and documentation to support management decision-making.
•	Manage internal and external communication channels, including the website, telephone systems, and email platforms.
•	Coordinate staff onboarding and induction processes, maintain employee records, and provide administrative support for human resources functions.
•	Liaise with staff, students, contractors, and external stakeholders to ensure effective communication and service delivery.
result.title: Office Manager

Our valued client Metal Recovery Industries based in Qld, is seeking an experienced Human Resources Officer to join their friendly team of professionals.

The Company collects, salvages and processes scrap metal goods for recycle and re use in regional and remote areas in Central North Queensland, including mining sites.

Main Purpose
The Human Resources (HR) Officer is responsible for delivering effective and compliant generalist human resources advisory and administration services to both internal and external stakeholders in accordance with relevant legislation and awards.

Key Duties/Responsibilities
Be the first point of contact for HR related queries
Participate and contribute to HR projects
Coordinate the end-to-end recruitment process
Place job advertisements and shortlist candidates
Conduct phone screening and interviews
Liaise with the hiring managers to place successful applicants
Draft and issue employment contracts and employment related letters
Coordinate the onboarding of new employees
Maintain employee files
Update and maintain the accuracy of HR registers
Provide support with HR monthly reports
Assist with organising Company events
Manage employment anniversaries and gifts
Provide general administrative support to the HR and Operations Teams as required
Support learning and development, performance management, remuneration and benefits activities and general HR duties
Facilitate and actively enhance employee life cycle processes
Stay up to date with changes to legislative compliance

Skills and Experience
Experience in a similar role within a HR function
Knowledge of Fair Work Act, Modern Awards, National Employment Standards and basic knowledge of industrial relations legislation
Strong interpersonal, verbal and written skills
Ability to work cooperatively and independently, whilst establishing positive relationships across the business
Excellent organisational and time management skills, with high attention to detail

result.description: LITTLE ENVIRONEERS PTY LTD  Little Environeers is seeking an enthusiastic and qualified Early Childhood Teacher to join our team in Macleod, Vic, 3085. This is an exciting opportunity for an educator who is passionate about inspiring young learners through engaging educational experiences. The successful candidate will be responsible for planning and delivering high-quality learning programs, supporting children's development, and fostering positive relationships with families and colleagues within a collaborative early learning environment.   Benefits   Competitive salary of $75,000–$90,000 plus superannuation.  Secure full-time permanent employment.  Supportive, friendly and collaborative team environment.  Ongoing professional development and career progression opportunities.  Modern learning spaces with high-quality educational resources.  Opportunity to make a meaningful impact on children's early learning and development.  Inclusive workplace that values innovation, creativity and diversity.  Strong commitment to employee wellbeing and work-life balance.  Stable employment with a respected and growing early childhood education provider.    Task & responsibilities   Plan, develop and implement engaging educational programs that promote children's literacy, numeracy, language, creativity, music, art and early learning skills.  Design stimulating indoor and outdoor learning experiences using a variety of educational resources and play-based teaching approaches.  Deliver activities that encourage children's cognitive, physical, emotional, social and creative development while building confidence and independence.  Foster language and communication skills through storytelling, songs, rhymes, role play, discussions and interactive group experiences.  Observe, assess and document children's learning, behaviour and developmental progress, identifying any concerns that may require further support.  Monitor children's health, nutrition, wellbeing and safety while maintaining a secure and supportive learning environment.  Communicate regularly with families regarding children's progress, achievements and individual learning goals.  Participate in parent-teacher meetings, staff meetings, professional development sessions and centre planning activities.  Contribute to family engagement initiatives and community participation programs that strengthen relationships with children and families.  Mentor and support student teachers and educators undertaking professional placements where required.  Plan and deliver activities that promote the development of speech, reading, writing, motor coordination, problem-solving and positive social interaction.  Maintain compliance with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF), National Quality Standard (NQS), child safety requirements and all relevant education regulations.  Ensure all teaching practices meet workplace health and safety standards and contribute to a positive, inclusive and respectful learning environment.    Qualification & experience   1–3 years of relevant experience as an Early Childhood Teacher is essential.  A completed relevant qualification in Early Childhood Education that meets Australian regulatory requirements is required.  Current teacher registration or licensing is required where applicable.  Sound knowledge of the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and National Quality Standard (NQS).  Excellent communication, interpersonal and organisational skills.  Ability to develop engaging educational programs that support children's learning and wellbeing.  Strong observation, planning and assessment skills.  Ability to work effectively both independently and within a collaborative team.  Commitment to child safety, inclusion and continuous professional development.   About Company    Little Environeers is a vibrant early learning centre committed to providing high-quality education and care for children in a safe, nurturing and inclusive environment. Our play-based learning programs encourage curiosity, creativity and confidence while supporting every child's social, emotional, cognitive and physical development. We value strong partnerships with families and believe in creating meaningful learning experiences that prepare children for lifelong success. Our dedicated educators work collaboratively to deliver exceptional outcomes in accordance with Australia's early childhood education standards.
